title: Multi-Cancer Early Screening with Non-contrast CT and Deep Learning.
summary: PANDA reports high pancreatic-lesion detection performance across large CT cohorts, including higher sensitivity and specificity than average radiologists.
source_collection: ITU AI for Good: Innovate for Impact (2025)
account: Alibaba DAMO reports validation involving 6,239 patients across ten centers and another cohort of 20,530 patients. The source states that PANDA exceeded mean radiologist sensitivity by 34.1% and specificity by 6.3% for pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma identification. These are diagnostic-performance findings, not quantified survival gains or a described individual treatment outcome.
purpose: Improve early cancer detection from non-contrast CT images.

ratings.reason: The study reports detection performance, but does not quantify treatment, health, or survival improvements for the people screened.
PANDA reportedly exceeds mean radiologist sensitivity by 34.1% and specificity by 6.3% for pancreatic cancer identification, supporting improved diagnostic capability in the evaluated cohorts.
Lives saved and population screening benefits are asserted downstream possibilities.

ai_role.statement: The contributor describes the system and its proposed or reported contribution. This collection entry does not independently isolate the effect of AI from the surrounding workflow.

evidence.citation: Contributed use case in International Telecommunication Union, AI for Good: Innovate for Impact, 2025. Information current as of June 2025. The reported outcomes are attributed to the submitting project, not an independent outcome evaluation by ITU.
evidence.title: Use Case 27: Multi-Cancer Early Screening with Non-contrast CT and Deep Learning.
